name: Microsoft Zaragoza (Puerto Venecia) datacenter campus
summary: Planned Microsoft datacenter campus in the city of Zaragoza beside the Puerto Venecia shopping area, one of three campuses in the PIGA Región MSFT regional plan. The November 2025 plan assigns it 57 hectares and about EUR 1.44 billion, with 50 MW secured for a first phase and up to 300 MW sought later via the Torrero-Valdeconsejo substation. The regional government declared it of general interest in September 2025 and began expropriating about 16.5 hectares of private land. Landowners and the ZeC party contested the project in 2026. Microsoft says only land clearing is authorized until the plan receives final approval.

location.note: Nominatim point for Puerto Venecia (Torrero-La Paz district); sources place the campus next to Puerto Venecia and Parque Venecia, but the parcel boundary is not published.

parties.name: Gobierno de Aragón
parties.note: Declared the campus of general interest, started expropriation and is processing the PIGA regional plan.

metrics.note: Per-site figure in the November 2025 PIGA as reported by elDiario.es.
Second-phase aspiration per campus in the PIGA, as reported by elDiario.es; Forbes gives 250-300 MW per campus over about ten years.
elDiario.es reported in August 2026 that about 16.5 hectares of private land at the site were being expropriated.

milestones.note: Regional government declared the campus of general interest and opened expropriation of private land.
Initial approval of the PIGA Región MSFT plan covering La Muela, Villamayor de Gállego and Zaragoza, opening a public information period.
A modification of the PIGA was published in the Boletín Oficial de Aragón for public comment; the ZeC party filed 25 objections citing trees, flood risk and water and energy use.
Forbes reported the first phase was expected to operate from 2030; Microsoft's plan foresees about four years for the first phase after final approval.

power_sources.description: Grid supply through the Torrero-Valdeconsejo substation, starting at 132 kV with a later upgrade to 220 kV.
